See also: órgano, organò, and organo-

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
organo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from Latin organum, from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon, “an organ of the body; a musical instrument, an organ”). Doublet of orgeno.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /orˈɡano/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ano
  • Syllabification: or‧ga‧no

Noun

[edit]

organo (accusative singular organon, plural organoj, accusative plural organojn)

  1. (anatomy) organ

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • cerbo (“brain”)
  • haŭto (“skin”)
  • hepato (“liver”)
  • intesto (“intestine”)
  • koro (“heart”)
  • pulmo (“lung”)
  • reno (“kidney”)
  • stomako (“stomach”)
  • veziko (“bladder”)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • ĉeforgano (“CPU, mainframe”)

See also

[edit]
  • orgeno (“organ (musical instrument)”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “organo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “organo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto organo, English organ, French organe, German Organ, Italian organo, Russian о́рган (órgan), Spanish órgano, all ultimately from Latin organum, from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵ-.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /orˈɡa.no/

Noun

[edit]

organo (plural organi)

  1. (anatomy) organ
  2. (law, institutional) organ, institution
  3. (figuratively) someone who expresses the thoughts, opinions, feelings of someone else (in newspapers etc.)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • organeto (“organelle”)
  • organala (“organic”)
  • organaro (“plant”)
  • organizar (“to organize”)
  • organizo (“organization”)
  • organizala (“organizational”)
  • organizuro (“organization, plant”)
  • organizero (“organizer”)
  • organizeso (“organization, plant”)

Interlingua

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

organo (plural organos)

  1. organ

Related terms

[edit]
  • organic

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Probably borrowed from Latin organum, from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon), derived from Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- (“to make”). Cf. the doublet argano.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɔr.ɡa.no/
  • Rhymes: -ɔrɡano
  • Hyphenation: òr‧ga‧no

Noun

[edit]

organo m (plural organi)

  1. organ (all senses)
  2. panel
  3. (anatomy) organ

Derived terms

[edit]
  • organello
  • organetto
  • organico
  • organigramma
  • organismo
  • organista
  • organistico
  • organizzare
  • organogenesi
  • organogeno
  • organografia
  • organoide
  • organolettico
  • organologia
  • organometallo
  • organopatia
  • organoscopia
  • organoterapia
  • organulo

Further reading

[edit]
  • organo in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Anagrams

[edit]
  • gorano, ognora, onagro, ongaro, orango, rogano

Latin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

organō

  1. dative/ablative singular of organum

References

[edit]
  • "organo", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish órgano.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈʔoɾɡano/ [ˌʔoɾ.ɡɐˈn̪o]
  • Rhymes: -oɾɡano
  • Syllabification: or‧ga‧no

Noun

[edit]

órganó (Baybayin spelling ᜂᜇ᜔ᜄᜈᜓ)

  1. (music) organ (a musical instrument made of multiple pipes)
  2. (anatomy, biology) organ (a larger part of an organism)
    Synonym: tatag
  3. mouthpiece; organ of information
    Synonyms: pamalita, bibig
  4. newspaper; magazine
    Synonyms: pahayagan, peryodiko, diyaryo

Related terms

[edit]
  • organista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “organo”, in Pambansang Diksiyonaryo | Diksiyonaryo.ph, 2018
